description: Uranium is a silvery-grey metal in the actinide series with atomic number 92. It is radioactive and has the highest atomic weight of naturally occurring elements, with a density about 70% higher than lead. It occurs naturally in low concentrations in soil, rock, and water.
uses: Uranium is used in nuclear power plants and nuclear weapons because uranium-235 is the only naturally occurring fissile element present in significant amounts. Civilian applications include fueling nuclear reactors to produce electricity, and historical uses include colorants for glass and pottery glazes. Depleted uranium is used in kinetic energy penetrators, armor plating, shielding materials, and as counterweights in aircraft.
characteristics: Uranium is a silvery white, weakly radioactive metal with a Mohs hardness of 6, sufficient to scratch glass. It is malleable, ductile, slightly paramagnetic, and a poor electrical conductor with a very high density of 19.1 g/cm³. It reacts with almost all non-metallic elements except noble gases, and its reactivity increases with temperature.
